Subject: Questionnaire: Isolated deployment controls and install process

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As part of our procurement packet I was asked to collect a concise answers pack for on-prem, fully isolated installations. Attached is MedSys's information-security questionnaire (Q1–Q28). Could you please: 1) confirm whether Redwood supports fully air-gapped installs with customer-managed key material, 2) list expected network flows for a VPC-only deployment, and 3) provide a preliminary SBOM and patching cadence?

We'd like to review your response with our engineering and security teams by Oct 20. If you need a short follow-up call, please propose slots next week.

Best,
Alex
Alex Reynolds
Head of Procurement, MedSys Health

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@medsys.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questionnaire: Isolated deployment controls and install process

Alex —

Thanks for sending this over. We can support fully isolated (air-gapped) deployments with customer-controlled keys and no outbound connectivity from the inference cluster. Attached is a short install plan and an initial network diagram that describes the recommended deployment boundaries and ingress/egress chokepoints.

High level answers:
- Yes, we support air-gapped/private deployments. Customer retains KMS/HSM and we provide integration adapters (PKCS#11, KMIP) that run inside the private network.
- Network flows: we recommend a management jump host in a DMZ for deployment only, and our control plane (if used) can be run as a separate customer-managed control plane. The diagram shows optional telemetry collectors — we recommend these be routed to a secured ops VPC if telemetry is required.
- SBOM: attached snapshot (redwood-sbom) for the runtime and kernel modules; we will supply a full SBOM under NDA.

CC'ing Vanessa and Markus for technical detail and the patching cadence. We'll aim to send the completed questionnaire by Oct 16. If that timing is tight for you, let us know.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Enterprise Ops 
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questionnaire: Isolated deployment controls and install process

Alex / team —

Following up with the technical responses inline against MedSys Q1–Q28 (see excerpted responses below). I'll attach a controlled patch schedule spreadsheet and a short runbook stub for OS/kernel patching and runtime updates.

Excerpted technical responses (high level):
Q3 (Key management): We integrate with customer HSMs via KMIP or PKCS#11. Keys never leave the customer boundary. For FIPS/HSM-backed signing of model artifacts we support an offline signing step.
Q7 (Outbound telemetry): By default the runtime emits zero outbound telemetry. Customers may enable encrypted batched telemetry to a customer-controlled collector; otherwise telemetry is stored locally and flushed via manual export.
Q12 (Software composition): We provide an SBOM export (CSV) for all runtime components; the snapshot is attached. Third-party binaries are tracked and updated on a quarterly cadence or per-critical CVE policy.
Q18 (Patching windows): We support scheduled maintenance windows and offer two patch streams: security-critical (applied ASAP within a customer-approved emergency window) and scheduled (quarterly). Patch binaries can be provided on removable media or via a signed package repository hosted inside the customer network.

Attachments included: sbom_snapshot_20261014.csv, controlled_patch_windows.xlsx, network_diagram_isolated_v2.png

If you'd like deeper detail on our offline attestation or SBOM provenance model, Markus can add a short note.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Vanessa —

Thanks for the detailed answers. A couple clarifications from our security team after reviewing the SBOM excerpt:
1) For offline signing you mentioned an "offline signing step" — can you describe who holds the build artifacts and where the signing takes place? Is there support for reproducible builds?
2) For patch delivery via removable media: can you outline checksum and provenance verification steps? We need guarantees that media delivered to our air-gapped sites will be verifiable before execution.

Also — are there any automated rollback mechanisms if a runtime update causes regression?

Regards,
Thomas Ng
Security Architect, MedSys Health

Thomas / Alex —

Good questions — answering succinctly:
1) Offline signing and build provenance: Our recommended pattern is that MedSys builds model artifacts internally. Redwood supplies a reproducible build recipe and a signing helper that runs inside your build environment. The artifact owner (MedSys) performs signing with your HSM; Redwood verifies signatures during install. We also provide a reproducible-build checklist and deterministic packaging guidance to minimize non-determinism.
2) Removable media verification: Each release bundle is published with SHA-512 checksums and a detached signature (created by the customer's HSM or by Redwood under NDA). On import, the install agent verifies checksum + detached signature before any extraction. We document the exact verification commands in the runbook.
3) Rollback: The runtime supports atomic canary-style rollouts with a pinned previous version that can be swapped in under failure conditions. We also provide a snapshot-and-rollback script that captures KV cache and model pointers to accelerate rollback. Rollbacks can be performed offline by following the runbook steps.

Next steps:
- We'll send the completed filled questionnaire PDF and the deployment_runbook_stub.md (attached).
- If agreeable, let's schedule a 30-minute technical review with your security team — propose Oct 22 or Oct 23 (10:00–13:00 PT) and we'll confirm.

Thanks for the thorough review — happy to iterate further.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Enterprise Ops
Redwood Inference
